properties.natural_language: Any block received from a block producer must have its block header fully validated against consensus rules before the fork activation check is performed.
Block header data received from an untrusted block producer must include a valid block number that can be compared against the activation threshold (7280000).
Blocks received from peer nodes for validation must be verified against the appropriate ruleset (pre-fork or ProgPoW) based on their block number before acceptance.
After applying ProgPoW rules at or above block 7280000, the network must transition to the post-fork state with ProgPoW consensus permanently enabled.
The fork activation threshold (block 7280000) is immutable; the check must deterministically route to either pre-fork or post-fork rules based solely on block number comparison.
All nodes must apply identical fork activation logic to prevent chain splits between upgraded and non-upgraded nodes.
Block validation must always use the correct ruleset for the block's height: pre-fork rules for blocks below 7280000 and ProgPoW rules at or above, regardless of network peer claims.
Block timestamps and heights used for fork activation must be derived from validated chain state and not from unverified external inputs.
Before any gas charge operation, evm.gas_left must be a non-negative integer representing available gas for the current execution context.
After a successful gas charge, evm.gas_left must be reduced by exactly the amount charged and must remain non-negative.
When gas is insufficient for an operation, an OutOfGasError must be raised and execution must halt; no partial gas deduction is allowed.
Memory cost calculation must follow the quadratic formula: total_cost = (words * 3) + (words^2 / 512), ensuring memory expansion is always more expensive at larger sizes.
Memory extension cost must always be incremental (new_total - old_total), never negative, ensuring memory costs are monotonically increasing with size.
Blob gas pricing must use an independent gas market from execution gas; blob base fee is computed from excess_blob_gas using the Taylor exponential function and is always >= MIN_BLOB_GASPRICE (1).
All nodes must compute blob base fee identically using the same exponential approximation function to maintain consensus.
The 63/64 gas reservation rule must always be applied for CALL/DELEGATECALL/STATICCALL, ensuring at least 1/64th of gas is retained by the calling context to prevent unbounded call depth attacks.
After a value-transferring CALL, the gas cost must include GAS_CALL_VALUE (9000) and the callee must receive GAS_CALL_STIPEND (2300) as additional gas.
Cold storage access must always cost more than warm access (2100 vs 100 gas for SLOAD), and first access to any slot must be treated as cold.
After a storage write from non-zero to zero, a gas refund of GAS_STORAGE_CLEAR_REFUND (4800) must be added to the transaction refund counter.
Integer arithmetic for all gas calculations must not overflow within the bounds of valid transactions; gas values must remain within uint256 range.
Excess blob gas defaults to 0 at fork activation and cannot go negative; it is clamped to max(0, parent_excess + parent_used - TARGET_BLOB_GAS_PER_BLOCK).
A block received from a network peer must pass header validation (gas metrics, difficulty, parent hash) before ommer validation or body execution proceeds.
Blocks from untrusted network peers must have all data independently validated; no block data is accepted without full consensus verification.
Transaction senders must be authenticated via signature recovery, and the sender account must be an EOA with correct nonce and sufficient balance before execution.
After block body execution, computed state root, transaction root, receipt root, and logs bloom must all match the values in the block header; any mismatch invalidates the block.
After ommer validation, the block must contain at most 2 ommers, each unique, aged 1-6 blocks, with valid parent, and not part of the canonical chain.
After extracting and pre-warming an access list, all specified addresses and storage keys must be marked warm in the access set before transaction execution begins.
Gas refund is always capped at 50% of total gas consumed by the transaction, preventing excessive refund exploitation.
Duplicate entries in access lists must be deduplicated during processing; each address/slot is marked warm only once regardless of repetition.
Cold access always costs more than warm access: cold account = 2600 gas, cold slot = 2100 gas, warm access = 100 gas as per EIP-2929.
After cold access, the accessed address/slot must be marked warm for all subsequent accesses within the same transaction.
Block reward must always be exactly 2 ETH plus ommer bonuses, paid to the coinbase address upon block finalization.
Transaction validation must check all conditions sequentially: gas availability, sender recovery, nonce match, balance sufficiency, and EOA status. Failure at any step must reject the transaction.
PoW validation must verify both mix digest and difficulty target; failure of either check must result in block rejection.
After difficulty calculation, the bomb delay of 9,000,000 blocks must be subtracted from the block number before computing the exponential bomb component.
Access list gas costs must accurately reflect actual storage access cost to prevent economic DoS attacks through mispriced operations.
Before SHA256 precompile execution, sufficient gas must be available: at least GAS_SHA256 (60) + GAS_SHA256_WORD (12) * ceil32(len(data))/32.
SHA256 precompile must always produce exactly 32 bytes of output regardless of input size, including for empty input.
The SHA256 hash function must be deterministic: identical inputs must always produce identical 32-byte outputs across all nodes.
After successful SHA256 execution, evm.output must contain exactly the 32-byte SHA256 digest of the input data.
Gas cost for SHA256 must be proportional to input size (base + per-word), ensuring large inputs cannot be processed below actual computational cost.
The ceil32() function must correctly round up input length to the nearest 32-byte boundary for word count calculation.
SHA256 precompile must accept arbitrary bytes as input, including empty input, without rejecting any input format.
SHA256 is assumed to be collision-resistant and preimage-resistant; contracts relying on hash-based commitments depend on this cryptographic property.
Before resolving a precompile address, the system must determine whether the address falls in the EIP range (0x01-0xff) or the RIP range (0x100-0x1ff).
EIP precompile addresses (0x01-0xff) and RIP precompile addresses (0x100-0x1ff) must never overlap; address separation guarantees no collision between L1 and L2 precompiles.
Smart contracts calling precompile addresses must have their calls resolved based on the address range; calls to unimplemented addresses in reserved ranges must behave as calls to empty accounts.
The 256-address RIP reservation (0x100-0x1ff) must be sufficient for all anticipated L2 precompile needs; exhaustion requires governance intervention.
L2 rollups must coordinate via the RIP governance process to avoid deploying conflicting precompiles at the same address, as no on-chain enforcement exists.
Input to the point evaluation precompile must be exactly 192 bytes; any other length must immediately raise KZGProofError.
The KZG commitment must be a valid 48-byte G1 point, the proof a valid 48-byte G1 point, and z and y must be valid BLS12-381 field elements (< BLS_MODULUS).
Before KZG proof verification, the versioned hash computed from the commitment must match the input versioned hash; mismatch triggers KZGProofError.
On successful KZG proof verification, the output must be exactly 64 bytes containing FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB (4096) and BLS_MODULUS encoded as 32-byte big-endian values.
The point evaluation precompile has a fixed gas cost of 50000; insufficient gas results in OutOfGasError before any cryptographic computation.
All error conditions (length mismatch, hash mismatch, proof failure, crypto exceptions) must converge to KZGProofError, providing uniform error handling.
The KZG trusted setup ceremony must have been performed correctly with toxic waste destroyed; compromise would allow forging arbitrary proofs.
Version byte 0x01 in versioned hashes must uniquely identify KZG commitments; future commitment schemes must use different version bytes to prevent type confusion.
Attackers must not be able to solve the discrete logarithm problem on BLS12-381; the KZG commitment scheme security depends on this hardness assumption.
RANDAO values retrieved from the beacon chain must be authentic and provided via the trusted consensus-execution client interface.
Block proposers providing RANDAO contributions must be authenticated via validator keys, though their intent to bias outcomes is not trusted.
After the PoS merge, opcode 0x44 must push the RANDAO mix from the block header mixHash field onto the stack; pre-merge it must push the traditional difficulty value.
A malicious proposer can influence RANDAO by at most 1 bit per controlled slot, at the cost of forfeited block rewards.
PREVRANDAO values exceeding 2^64 serve as a heuristic to detect PoS execution context, but must not be relied upon for critical security decisions.
Applications requiring unpredictable randomness must use commit-reveal schemes with at minimum a 4-epoch (~25.6 minute) delay when using PREVRANDAO.
After populating the mixHash field, the block header must contain the RANDAO mix value retrieved from the parent beacon block state.
EIP proposals submitted by untrusted authors must undergo core developer evaluation before being considered for inclusion in the Glamsterdam upgrade.
Client teams configuring activation times must coordinate across all Ethereum client implementations to prevent inconsistent activation causing chain splits.
EIP lifecycle must follow a strict state machine: Proposed -> Considered -> (Scheduled | Declined). No EIP can skip the consideration phase.
Network upgrades must follow the standard activation sequence: Sepolia testnet, Holesky testnet, then mainnet, to validate changes on testnets first.
EIPs listed as scheduled for inclusion must actually be implemented and activated as planned; deviations require governance process updates.
Withdrawal requests to the predeploy contract must include msg.value >= current_fee; insufficient fee must cause the transaction to fail.
Calldata to the withdrawal predeploy must be exactly 0 bytes (fee query) or exactly 56 bytes (validator pubkey + amount); any other length must result in failure.
Any external caller can invoke the withdrawal predeploy, but msg.sender must be recorded as source_address for consensus layer credential validation.
After consensus layer processing, withdrawal requests must be authorized only if source_address matches the validator's 0x01 withdrawal credentials.
The withdrawal request fee must follow an exponential pricing model: MIN_FEE * e^(excess / UPDATE_FRACTION), always >= MIN_WITHDRAWAL_REQUEST_FEE (1 wei).
At most MAX_WITHDRAWAL_REQUESTS_PER_BLOCK (16) requests can be dequeued per block via the system call.
The withdrawal queue must be FIFO-ordered: requests are added at the tail and removed from the head, preserving submission order.
The predeploy contract at address 0x00000961Ef480Eb55e80D19ad83579A64c007002 must be correctly deployed and immutable; missing or corrupted contract causes block validation failure.
The exponential fee mechanism must prevent indefinite spam of withdrawal requests; fees grow exponentially with excess demand above the target rate of 2 per block.
After system call dequeue, requests must be included in the ExecutionPayload for consensus layer processing within the same block.
Existing custody arrangements relying on withdrawal credentials not being able to trigger exits must be renegotiated before EIP-7002 activation.
Blocks from untrusted miners must have their difficulty value validated against the expected difficulty computed using the correct formula (original or adjusted) based on block height.
Blocks received from peer nodes must have their stated difficulty independently computed and verified; any mismatch must result in block rejection.
After fork activation, the fake block number must be computed as max(0, block.number - 11,400,000) for the difficulty bomb calculation.
The fork activation is deterministic: all nodes must switch to the adjusted difficulty formula at exactly FORK_BLOCK_NUMBER to prevent chain splits.
The fake block number must never be negative; the max(0, ...) guard ensures that for blocks below 11,400,000, the bomb calculation uses block 0.
After difficulty validation, blocks with matching difficulty are accepted and blocks with mismatching difficulty are rejected.
The 11.4 million block offset must provide sufficient delay for planned network upgrades (The Merge); if delayed, another difficulty bomb delay EIP would be required.
Pre-fork blocks must use the actual block number for difficulty calculation; only post-fork blocks use the adjusted (fake) block number.
